title: AI and systems for restaurants in Flagstaff
meta_description: Creosote Labs in Flagstaff builds scheduling, inventory, and ordering systems, restaurant websites, and staff AI training for Flagstaff restaurants.
h1: Restaurants in Flagstaff: AI, systems, and websites
intro: Restaurants in Flagstaff generally run the front of house on a point-of-sale system such as Toast or Square, take reservations through OpenTable, Resy, or the phone, and schedule staff in 7shifts or a shared spreadsheet. Invoices from food and beverage vendors, weekly inventory counts, catering orders, and private event contracts are often handled on paper or in a manager's email, and menu changes have to be updated in the POS, on the website, and on third-party delivery platforms separately.

Creosote Labs is a Flagstaff company and works with restaurants here on site. A one-day operations review covers ordering, inventory, scheduling, catering, and the website, and produces a written assessment with a quote for each recommendation. Typical implementation connects vendor invoices to a single cost tracker, builds a catering and event request form, and keeps the menu in one place that updates the website and online ordering. Staff training covers using AI for menus, descriptions, and guest correspondence.
projects: A menu management tool that holds every item and price once and publishes changes to the website and online ordering.
A vendor invoice pipeline that reads Sysco, US Foods, and local supplier invoices into a weekly food cost report.
A catering and private event request form that collects headcount, date, and menu selections and produces a quote and contract.
A restaurant website with hours, the current menu, reservations, and online ordering links in one place.
An inventory count sheet that staff fill in on a phone and that flags items below par for the next order.
A one-day training in which managers use AI to write menu descriptions, respond to reviews, and draft staff communications.

faqs.q: Can this work with the POS system already in use?
faqs.a: Toast and Square both provide reporting exports and integration options, and the operations review establishes what the restaurant's plan supports. We build around the existing POS rather than replacing it.

faqs.q: When does the on-site work happen?
faqs.a: The operations review is a single day, and we schedule it around service. Observation of a lunch or dinner shift is useful, and the desk work with the owner or general manager can happen during off hours.

The operations review is $3,000 and delivers a quote for each recommendation. Systems and websites are quoted fixed price with no hourly billing. Team AI training is priced at $1,000 per participant, with a minimum of 5 participants.
